# Agent Community — Bots for DeepSeek Harness
**Persistent Bots, group rooms and a durable run ledger, inside DSH.**
简体中文 · Design notes · MIT
> A community-maintained DeepSeek Harness plugin, not an official DeepSeek product.
A Bot here is not a temporary subagent: it has an identity, its own model and permission preset, its

own
workspace, and its own session that survives a restart. Put several of them in a room and they

answer
together. Every run is recorded, so a conversation can be read back later even after the sess

ion that
produced it is gone.
## Features
- **Bots that persist.** Each Bot keeps a name, a model, a permission preset and a workspace on disk

. It
is listed in the panel and answers in any room it belongs to, before and after a restart.
- **O

ne-to-one and group conversations.** A room is a list of members. A message addressed to one Bot
rou
tes to that Bot; a message addressed to nobody in particular is answered by every member, because a

greeting is addressed to the room.
- **Runs are queued, leased and recoverable.** Each answer is a r

un with a lease and a heartbeat. A run
whose runtime dies is reclaimed instead of blocking the room,

and a room keeps working while you do
something else.
- **A durable transcript.** The panel draws f

rom a ledger written as the run happens (messages, tool
calls and their results, approvals, errors),

not from the session log. Compacted-away history is
replaced by a summary rather than silently drop

ped.
- **15 model-facing tools**, so a Bot can create rooms, hand work to another Bot, decompose a r

equest
into tasks and report on them: `agent_community_create_bot`, `agent_community_update_bot`,
`a

gent_community_list_bots`, `agent_community_create_room`, `agent_community_send_message`,
`agent_com

munity_list_runs`, `agent_community_get_context`, `agent_community_post_message`,
`agent_community_t

ask_decompose`, `agent_community_task_assign`, `agent_community_task_status`,
`agent_community_task_

report`, `agent_community_submit_final`, `agent_community_remember`,
`agent_community_deliver`.
- **
Models come from DSH Settings.** The Bot form and the composer's model menu read the deployment's li

ve
catalog — every provider, every model, its display name and its reasoning levels. Nothing about a

vendor
or a model is hard-coded; a provider added or renamed in Settings appears without restarting

.
- **File cards for what a Bot delivered.** A Bot declares the files it produced with
`agent_commun

ity_deliver`; the turn then shows file cards below its reply — preview in the panel,
open with the O

S application association, or reveal in Finder. Files may live inside the Bot's
workspace or at any

absolute path.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.1-rc.2` (built and verified against it; no DSH version is pinned) |
| Node

.js | `^22.19.0` or `>=24` |
| pnpm | `11.7.0` (for building from source) |
`@deepseek-ai/*` packages are **not** published to the public npm registry, so this repo cannot inst

all
them and `pnpm install` alone fails — expected. The plugin deliberately does **not** pin a DSH v

ersion:
every peer range is `*` and a missing host package degrades at load instead of failing the i

nstall. That
is also why the plugin is meant to be installed *into* a DSH profile, where the running

harness supplies
those packages.

estart DSH and refresh the page — **Bots团队** appears in the sidebar.

The archive attached to each release is the same build that is published to npm — use it when you
wo

uld rather not install through a registry. The line below points at the latest public release;
see C
HANGELOG.md for what a newer version changes.

### Installing from a checkout instead
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Keep the `file:` prefix. pnpm records a bare absolute path as a `link:` symlink and then installs no

ne of
the bundle's own `file:` dependencies; the profile ends up with the bundle and no `@dsh-plugin

-agent-community/*` rows,
and every row fails to import. The same applies to DSH's own plugin manage

r, which passes an absolute
path through unchanged.

## Usage
| What you want | How |
| Create a Bot | Open **Bots团队** → **＋** → fill in name, model, permission and workspace. The Bot is

created immediately and appears in the roster. |
| Talk to one Bot | Select it in the **Bots** tab

(one-to-one room) and send a message. |
| Create a group | **＋** in the **群聊** tab, pick the members

. |
| Address one member of a group | Type `@` and pick a Bot from the menu, or use its name in the

text. Only that Bot is queued. |
| Address the whole room | Send a message that names nobody. Every

member answers. |
| Add a file or image | **＋** → **文件**, or paste/drop it onto the composer. |
| Ch

ange the model for one room | **＋** → **模型**. Affects the next run, not one already in flight. |
| C

hange a Bot's permission preset | **＋** → **权限**: 仅可查看 / 工作区内修改 / 完全权限. |
| Compress a long room | *

*＋** → **压缩**. Shows a summary row and keeps the newest messages. |
| Stop a run | **停止** in the tit

le bar cancels the room's active runs. |
[该节后续省略]
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bundle mounts all three; each package is also installable on its own — `core/agent-community` sh

ips
its own `cordis.patch.yml` and `dsh.bundle`, which is the right shape for a headless deployment.

See DESIGN.md for the UI decisions (DSH token system, DSH client primitives, `StateDot` for
